en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa: Dhammānuloma (1), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 3.14. Saraṇaduka, Tika [The following is the list of conditions: 1. Conditioned by the state that is a cause (hetu-dhamma), there arises a state that is a cause by root-condition (hetu-paccaya). 2. Conditioned by the state that is a cause, there arises a state that is not a cause by root-condition. 3. Conditioned by the state that is a cause, there arises a state that is both a cause and not a cause by root-condition. 4. Conditioned by the state that is not a cause, there arises a state that is not a cause by root-condition. 5. Conditioned by the state that is not a cause, there arises a state that is a cause by root-condition. 6. Conditioned by the state that is not a cause, there arises a state that is both a cause and not a cause by root-condition. 7. Conditioned by the state that is both a cause and not a cause, there arises a state that is a cause by root-condition. 8. Conditioned by the state that is both a cause and not a cause, there arises a state that is not a cause by root-condition. 9. Conditioned by the state that is both a cause and not a cause, there arises a state that is both a cause and not a cause by root-condition. [End of] Saraṇaduka, Tika.

Dependent upon a state that is non-conflict (*araṇa*), non-demonstrable (*anidassana*), and impinging (*sappaṭigha*), there arises a state that is non-conflict, non-demonstrable, and impinging, by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated.)

Under the root condition: one; under the predominance condition: one …pe… under the non-disappearance condition: one. (Abbreviated. (In the section on co-nascence …pe… and in the section on inquiry, it is one in every instance.

Dependent on a state that is without conflict (*araṇa*), non-manifesting and non-reacting, there arises a state that is without conflict, non-manifesting and non-reacting, by way of the root condition.
